newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka leaders hail accord aiming to end war.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka leaders hail accord aiming to end war.

text.p: Sri Lankan leaders on Thursday hailed a bipartisan agreement to work towards ending the country's ethnic war, saying it showed a change of attitude among politicians over the conflict.
"I hope it will be the beginning of an effort to solve this problem once and for all," President Chandrika Kumaratunga told government officials and diplomats in the capital Colombo.

Kumaratunga's People's Alliance and the main opposition United National Party (UNP) signed an agreement last week to work together to end a 13-year war with Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels.
Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar paid tribute to Wickremesinghe "for having risen above party politics of the day".
But he cautioned it was too early to discuss results of the agreement.
"In a long history of a problem, only the foolish will expect that on the morrow there is going to be some beautiful blossoms in the garden," he added.
The Sri Lankan government has said the agreement was not a prelude to foreign mediation in ending the war and that there were no immediate plans for talks with the LTTE.
An LTTE spokesman in London told Reuters on Wednesday the rebels had no plans for peace talks with Colombo.

The LTTE is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year, but the rebels say the toll is higher.
